sources.title: University of Washington, ME 544, Large-Eddy Simulation lecture notes, 8 May 2018 (29-page PDF)
sources.locator: §2 'Filtering', printed pp. 5–6 (filter Eq. (1), unit-mass normalization and derivative commutation Eq. (5)); §3 'Filtering the equations of motion', printed pp. 10–12 (filtered continuity/momentum and stress Eqs. (13)–(20), resolved kinetic-energy derivation Eqs. (23)–(24), and backscatter qualification). The full 29-page PDF is available; detailed reading recorded here is of these relevant sections.

contents.name: §2 filter definition and unit-mass normalization, printed p. 5, Eq. (1)
contents.support: Supports the normalized spatial-convolution convention. The item states the periodic kernel and its own proof establishes the exact torus normalization.

contents.name: §2 filter commutation and the variable-filter commutator, printed pp. 5–6, Eqs. (2) and (5)
contents.support: The notes require spatially homogeneous filtering for derivative commutation and display the extra term for spatially varying filters; the item proves the homogeneous periodic case under smoothness and compactness hypotheses.

contents.name: §3 filtered continuity, momentum, and residual stress, printed pp. 10–11, Eqs. (13)–(20)
contents.support: Supports filtering the incompressible equation, commutation of the fixed convolution with derivatives, and the exact residual stress with the declared index convention.

contents.name: §3 resolved kinetic-energy calculation and transfer/backscatter discussion, printed pp. 11–12, Eqs. (23)–(24)
contents.support: Supports the resolved-energy product-rule derivation and the warning that the local stress-transfer term can represent loss or gain. The carrier supplies the full periodic integration argument.

contents.name: Boundary and spatially varying filter commutator terms in §2, printed pp. 5–6, Eq. (5)
contents.reason: This pair proves only the homogeneous periodic convolution case; it does not assert a boundary-filter or variable-width commutator theorem.

sources.title: Gregory L. Eyink, The ‘Multifractal Model’ of Turbulence and A Priori Estimates in Large-Eddy Simulation, I. Subgrid Flux and Locality of Energy Transfer, arXiv:chao-dyn/9602018v1 (33-page PDF)
sources.locator: §1, printed pp. 2–3, Eqs. (1)–(4) for filtering and exact stress; §II 'A Priori Estimates and the Multifractal Model', printed pp. 5–8, Eqs. (9)–(25) for resolved energy, transfer sign, increment covariance, positivity under a nonnegative filter, and Hölder stress/flux bounds. Relevant complete arguments were read from the PDF.

contents.name: §1 filtering and exact filtered Navier–Stokes residual stress, printed pp. 2–3, Eqs. (1)–(4)
contents.support: Provides an independent LES formulation and the exact residual-stress convention. The item fixes its own periodic and dimensional conventions.

contents.name: §II local resolved-energy equation and forward-transfer sign, printed p. 5, Eqs. (9)–(11)
contents.support: Matches Pi=-grad(ubar):tau and identifies it as a local transfer term; no universal sign is claimed.

contents.name: §II increment covariance identity and its derivation, printed pp. 5–6, Eqs. (12)–(19)
contents.support: Supports the exact covariance form and the consequence that a nonnegative unit-mass filter gives a symmetric positive-semidefinite stress.

contents.name: §II Hölder stress and flux estimates with filter moment hypotheses, printed pp. 7–8, Eqs. (20)–(25)
contents.support: Supports the powers ell^(2 alpha), ell^(alpha-1), and ell^(3 alpha-1) under an explicit Hölder increment assumption and finite kernel moments; the carrier derives an explicit constant and time-integrated version.

contents.name: Multifractal phenomenology and later locality conclusions beyond the estimates used in §II
contents.reason: No multifractal statistical model, locality theorem, or empirical cascade claim is used as a mathematical premise in this batch.
